newsitem.title: PERU: Motorola sees $40 mln '97 revenues in Peru - paper.
newsitem.headline: Motorola sees $40 mln '97 revenues in Peru - paper.

text.p: U.S. telecommunications firm Motorola Inc expects total billing of $40 million in Peru throughout 1997, the daily Expreso said Wednesday.

Expreso quoted Motorola's vice-president and regional director of operations in Latin America and the Caribbean, Dan Przybylski, as saying he hoped Peru would contribute 10 percent of the company's revenue in the region.
He also said Peru's recent economic opening meant strong potential growth in the telecommunications field of around 100 percent annually for the next five years.
Motorola installed a Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) cellular telephone system in Peru last December, making it the first CDMA commercial service in Latin America.
The most popular Motorola products in Peru are radio communications, beepers and cellular phones, Expreso said.
